Think About This

When you were playing Minecraft or CodeCombat, how were you already thinking like a programmer?

Task: Turn and talk: share one example from your gameplay.

Computational Thinking

Computational thinking is how programmers solve problems. It has four parts:

Decomposition

Breaking a big problem into smaller, easier pieces.

Pattern Recognition

Finding similarities and repeating steps.

Abstraction

Focusing on what matters and ignoring what does not.

Algorithmic Thinking

Creating clear, step-by-step instructions.

1 Decomposition

What is it?

Breaking a big, complex problem into smaller, manageable pieces.

1 Decomposition

Minecraft Example

Big problem: Get the treasure from the underwater temple.

  1. Find a boat
  2. Sail to the temple
  3. Swim down carefully
  4. Avoid the guardians
  5. Collect the treasure
  6. Swim back up
In CodeCombat, how did you break down "defeat all the ogres"?

2 Pattern Recognition

What is it?

Finding things that repeat or are similar. This helps us save time.

CodeCombat Example

// You probably did this many times:
move right
move right
attack enemy
// This is a pattern: move, move, attack.

2 Pattern Recognition

Minecraft Example

Walk 3 steps, then turn. Repeat to make a square path.

What patterns did you notice when building paths or fighting enemies?

3 Abstraction

What is it?

Focusing on important details and ignoring things that do not matter right now.

3 Abstraction

Game Focus

What You Focused On What You Ignored
Where the enemy is The color of the grass
How many blocks to move The clouds in the sky
Which direction to turn The background music
When solving a puzzle level, what details were important? What could you ignore?

4 Algorithmic Thinking

What is it?

Creating a clear, step-by-step set of instructions anyone can follow.

Real Life Example: Make a Sandwich

START
GET two slices of bread
SPREAD butter on one slice
ADD cheese on top
PUT second slice on top
CUT sandwich in half
END

4 Algorithmic Thinking

Minecraft Example

The blocks you put together were an algorithm: instructions for the computer to follow.

Three Building Blocks of Code

Every program, no matter how complex, uses three basic ideas:

Sequence

Do things in order, one after another.

Selection

Make a choice: IF this, THEN do that.

Iteration

Repeat something multiple times.

All the games you played used these ideas. Let's see how.

Sequence

What is it?

Instructions that run in order, from top to bottom. The computer follows them one by one.

CodeCombat Example

MOVE right
MOVE right
ATTACK nearest enemy
MOVE down

Order matters. If you attack first, you might miss.

Sequence

Common Misconception

Wrong: "The computer can do many things at once."

Correct: "The computer does one thing at a time, in order."

Selection

What is it?

Making decisions in code. The program checks a condition and chooses what to do.

Minecraft and CodeCombat

IF there is an enemy in front
  THEN attack the enemy
  ELSE move forward
END IF

Selection

Real Life Example

IF it is raining
  THEN take an umbrella
  ELSE wear sunglasses
END IF
In your games, when did you need to make a choice? What condition did you check?

Iteration (Loops)

What is it?

Doing something over and over again. This saves us from writing the same code many times.

Minecraft Example

Without a loop (long and boring):

MOVE forward
MOVE forward
MOVE forward
MOVE forward
MOVE forward

Iteration (Loops)

With a loop (much better):

REPEAT 5 times
  MOVE forward
END REPEAT
Where in your games did you do the same action many times? Could a loop help?

Putting It All Together

A real program uses all three building blocks:

Example: Defeating Enemies in CodeCombat

// SEQUENCE: Start the program
START
// ITERATION: Keep going until all enemies are gone
REPEAT until no enemies left
  // SELECTION: Make a decision
  IF enemy is close
    THEN attack enemy
    ELSE move closer
  END IF
END REPEAT
// SEQUENCE: Finish
END

Common Misconceptions

Misconception 1: "The computer knows what I want"

Wrong: "I just need to put blocks together and the computer will figure it out."

Correct: "The computer only does exactly what I tell it to do. It cannot guess."

Example: If you tell the character to move forward but there is a wall, it will try and fail. The computer does not find another route.

When did your code fail because the computer did exactly what you said, not what you wanted?

More Misconceptions

Misconception 2: "Order does not matter"

Wrong: "I can put the blocks in any order and it will work."

Correct: "The computer reads code from top to bottom. Order is very important."

// This works
MOVE to enemy -> ATTACK enemy
// This does not work
ATTACK enemy -> MOVE to enemy

More Misconceptions

Misconception 3: "Loops go forever"

Wrong: "Once I start a loop, I cannot stop it."

Correct: "Loops repeat a specific number of times or until a condition is met."

How to Read Pseudocode

Pseudocode is not a real programming language. It is a way to write ideas in plain English.

Pseudocode Word What It Means Example
START / END Where the program begins and finishes Every program has these
IF / THEN / ELSE Making a decision IF hungry THEN eat
REPEAT / END REPEAT Do something multiple times REPEAT 3 times
// (comment) Notes for humans, not code // This explains the code

How to Read Pseudocode

Pseudocode has no strict rules. The important thing is that it is clear.

Answers

3. Sequence -> A. Moved, then attacked, then moved
